Position: Communication and Outreach Officer_UDAAN
Location: Bhakta Marga, Kathmandu, Nepal
Job Type: Full-time
Duration: One year (with possible extension based on project need)
Salary: NPR 65,000-70,000 (Gross, Negotiable)

About the organization

Youth Innovation Lab (YI-Lab) is a not-for-profit civic tech company that works at the intersection of emerging cutting-edge technological tools and their applications by equipping young professionals to solve emerging challenges in our community. YI-Lab’s mission statement is, ‘to engage young people to bridge science to people and policy through innovation’. YI-Lab harnesses indigenous knowledge, citizen science approach, develops low-cost technological solutions, promotes open data, promotes entrepreneurship, and conducts evidence-based advocacy campaigns. YI-Lab provides a conducive environment for young people to co-create solutions for inclusive development.

About the project

About the project: The UDAAN (Unleashing Digital Acceleration and Ambition of Nepali Youth) project, led by Youth Innovation Lab together with Heifer Project Nepal, NAAMII, and Women In Animation and supported by the European Union, is a nationwide initiative aimed at empowering young women and men across Nepal with the skills, opportunities, and resources needed to thrive in the digital economy.

Implemented over four years, the project focuses on advancing digital literacy, fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, and creating pathways to employment through training programs in AI, coding, and creative technologies, as well as internships, fellowships, and innovation hubs in partnership with local governments, academic institutions, and the private sector.

With a strong commitment to gender equality and social inclusion, UDAAN prioritizes marginalized and underrepresented youth, contributing to a more inclusive, resilient, and future-ready workforce in Nepal. The action is implemented through four interconnected components:

PATHSHALA – Digital Skills Development: Builds future-ready digital skills through AI, Coding, and Animation schools. Using tiered, hybrid learning, it prepares young Nepali women and men for jobs, innovation, and entrepreneurship in the digital economy.

KARYASHALA – Innovation and Experimentation: Transforms youth skills into real-world digital solutions through hackathons and bootcamps. It nurtures innovation with mentorship and incubation, turning ideas into scalable impact.

KARMASHALA – Employment and Career Pathways: Connects young Nepali youth to real-world work experience through internships and fellowships. It bridges skills to careers by placing youth in government and private sector roles, building employability and professional confidence.

NITISHALA – Policy and System Strengthening: Strengthens youth participation in digital governance through policy dialogues, innovation hubs, and civic engagement. It bridges youth, communities, and local governments to institutionalize inclusive and sustainable digital transformation.

Job Description

The Communication and Outreach Officer will lead the design and implementation of integrated communication, outreach, and engagement strategies for the UDAAN project.

The role will focus on increasing awareness, driving enrollment, strengthening stakeholder engagement, and amplifying the project’s visibility and impact through strategic communication, storytelling, and creative engagement initiatives, including podcast production and large-scale youth engagement events such as the Creator’s Carnival.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  •  Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Media, Marketing, Development Studies, or related field
  • 2–4 years of relevant experience in communication, outreach, or digital marketing
  •  Experience managing digital campaigns and content creation
  • Experience working with youth programs or development projects (preferred)
  • Experience in donor-funded projects is an advantage
  • Excellent communication, coordination, and reporting skills

Skills & Competencies

  •  Strong writing, storytelling, and content development skills
  • Digital marketing and social media management
  • Graphic design and multimedia skills (e.g., Canva, Adobe tools)
  • Ability to simplify complex/technical concepts for wider audiences
  •  Experience in podcast production, storytelling, or multimedia content creation
  • Experience in event design and youth engagement campaigns
  •  Strong coordination and interpersonal skills
  • Analytical skills for tracking communication performance
  •  Commitment to gender equality and social inclusion (GESI)
  •  Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali

Key Responsibilities

1. Communication Strategy & Campaign Management

  •  Develop and implement a comprehensive communication and outreach strategy aligned with project goals
  • Design and execute targeted campaigns for different audiences (youth, institutions, partners)
  • Ensure compliance with EU visibility and branding guidelines
  • Align communication efforts with program milestones and enrollment targets

2. Outreach & Participation Mobilization

  • Lead nationwide outreach strategies to ensure inclusive participation
  •  Engage with schools, colleges, youth networks, CSOs, and local governments
  •  Organize orientation sessions, info campaigns, and enrollment drives
  •  Ensure strong participation of women, rural youth, and marginalized communities

3. Content Development & Digital Communication

  •  Manage digital platforms and social media campaigns
  •  Develop high-quality content, including:
  • Social media posts and campaigns
  • Blogs, newsletters, and knowledge products
  • Success stories and testimonials
  • Multimedia content (graphics, videos, reels)
  •  Translate technical program content into accessible, youth-friendly messaging

4. Creative Engagement & Storytelling Initiatives

  •  Lead the design and implementation of a UDAAN podcast series, including:
  • Content planning and thematic development
  • Coordination with speakers, youth, and experts
  • Oversight of production, editing, and dissemination
  • Develop storytelling formats to showcase youth journeys, innovation, and impact
  •  Use creative media to enhance engagement and learning across project components

5. Events & Flagship Engagements

  •  Lead the planning and execution of outreach and engagement events, including the Creator’s Carnival
  • Design event concepts aligned with youth engagement and digital innovation goals
  • Coordinate logistics, partners, communication, and visibility for events
  •  Ensure inclusive participation and strong audience engagement

6. Media & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build and manage relationships with media, influencers, and partner organizations
  •  Coordinate press releases, media coverage, and public communication
  •  Strengthen partnerships to expand outreach and visibility

7. Documentation, Learning & Reporting

  •  Ensure high-quality documentation of activities through photos, videos, and stories
  •  Track communication performance (reach, engagement, conversions)
  •  Monitor outreach effectiveness and enrollment trends
  •  Prepare reports aligned with project MEL systems
  • Use insights to continuously improve communication strategies

Key Deliverables

  •  UDAAN communication and outreach strategy prepared within the first month and approved by the Project Lead.
  •  Monthly content and campaign calendar prepared and implemented.
  •  Monthly digital/social media performance report prepared, including reach, engagement, and enrollment-related insights.
  • Outreach and event communication plans and reports prepared for major activities, including the Creator’s Carnival.
  •  Stories, blogs, testimonials, photos, videos, and multimedia products developed with proper consent, GESI sensitivity, and branding compliance.

Reporting Line

The Communication and Outreach Officer will report to the Project Lead and work closely with program, technical, MEL, communications, and consortium teams. The Officer will provide regular updates through weekly coordination meetings, monthly communication performance reports, and campaign/event debriefs as required.

Application Process

We highly encourage all interested applicants, especially youth and young professionals and candidates from discriminated groups (women, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai, and other minority communities) to apply.

We are having interviews on a rolling basis and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview.

Deadline for submission of application: 8 September 2026 Nepal Time 11:59 PM

Posiiton: Brand and Business Development Manager

About the job

MV Dugar Auto Division is a leading mobility solutions provider in Nepal, representing global brands across two-wheelers, commercial vehicles, tractors, construction equipment and industrial tires. With a strong nationwide network, the division delivers premium products supported by reliable after-sales service and genuine spare parts. MV Dugar Auto Division is committed to delivering world-class mobility solutions while creating long-term value for customers, partners and stakeholders.

As part of our business diversification and growth strategy, MV Dugar Group is now expanding into the FMCG / Food & Beverage sector in Nepal. We are launching an established Indian FMCG brand with an initial portfolio spanning Ice Cream, Sauces, Condiments and Packaged Foods.

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced and commercially driven Brand & Business Development Manager to lead the development and growth of an established Indian FMCG company’s business in Nepal.

With an initial portfolio focused on Ice Cream, Sauces, Condiments and Packaged Foods, the company is entering an exciting phase of market development and expansion in Nepal.

This is a hands-on, entrepreneurial leadership role for a professional who can take ownership of building the brand and business from the ground up. The position will work closely with the Indian principal/company and the Nepal management team to translate an established brand into a successful and sustainable Nepal market operation.

The successful candidate will be responsible for market strategy, brand building, product localization, regulatory compliance, pricing, distribution, retail development and new product launches.

Key Responsibilities

1. Brand Development & Marketing

  • Develop the brand’s positioning, proposition and go-to-market strategy for the Nepalese market.
  • Build brand awareness and establish a strong market presence from the early stages of entry.
  • Adapt the Indian brand strategy to local consumer needs while maintaining overall brand identity and equity.
  • Develop annual brand, marketing, activation and communication plans.
  • Lead coordination with advertising agencies, creative partners, designers, digital agencies and other external stakeholders.
  • Plan and execute digital marketing, social media, influencer campaigns, consumer activations, sampling, events and retail promotions.
  • Develop marketing campaigns around product launches, seasonal opportunities and key consumption occasions.

2. Market & Product Strategy

  • Conduct market research and identify opportunities across ice cream, sauces, condiments and packaged food categories.
  • Analyze consumer preferences, emerging trends, competitive activity and market gaps.
  • Benchmark competitors on product offerings, flavors, pack sizes, pricing, positioning and distribution.
  • Recommend suitable products and SKUs from the Indian portfolio for launch in Nepal.
  • Identify opportunities for Nepal-specific products, pack formats or flavors.
  • Develop a structured product and category launch roadmap.

3. Regulatory Compliance & Product Registration

  • Take ownership of the Nepal-side regulatory and compliance requirements for commercializing food products.
  • Coordinate product registration, food licenses, laboratory testing, certifications and other required approvals.
  • Ensure products and packaging comply with applicable Nepalese food regulations.
  • Review ingredient declarations, nutritional information, allergen declarations, manufacturing details, batch information, MRP, expiry dates and other mandatory labelling requirements.
  • Coordinate with relevant government authorities, laboratories, regulatory consultants and the Indian principal.
  • Maintain comprehensive and organized regulatory documentation for each SKU.
  • Monitor relevant changes in food regulations and ensure ongoing compliance.

4. Product & Packaging Localization

  • Work closely with the Indian principal/manufacturer to adapt products for the Nepal market.
  • Recommend appropriate product formats, pack sizes and SKU assortments.
  • Coordinate Nepal-specific packaging and labelling requirements.
  • Manage packaging artwork development, review and approval.
  • Ensure all regulatory and commercial information is accurate prior to production.
  • Provide market insights and consumer feedback to Indian product development and manufacturing teams.

5. Pricing & Commercial Strategy

  • Develop an effective pricing architecture for the Nepal market.
  • Analyze landed costs, taxes, distributor margins, retailer margins, promotional costs and overall profitability.
  • Benchmark pricing against local, Indian and international competitors.
  • Recommend appropriate MRP and channel-specific pricing strategies.
  • Develop trade schemes, introductory offers and promotional programmes in coordination with the sales function.
  • Monitor commercial performance and identify opportunities to improve margins and market competitiveness.

6. Distribution & Retail Development

Develop and support the go-to-market strategy across:

  • General Trade
  • Modern Trade
  • Supermarkets
  • Hotels, Restaurants & Cafés (HoReCa)
  • Institutional Customers
  • E-commerce and Quick Commerce, where relevant

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Identifying and onboarding distributors, dealers and channel partners.
  • Developing relationships with major retailers and key accounts.
  • Supporting distribution expansion across priority markets.
  • Preparing retailer presentations, product catalogues and sales materials.
  • Monitoring product availability, visibility, merchandising and execution.
  • Working closely with sales and distribution partners to improve product availability and sell-through.

7. Product Launch & Market Execution

  • Develop comprehensive launch plans for the company and individual products.
  • Coordinate product availability, distribution, marketing and retail activation ahead of launch.
  • Plan and execute sampling programmes, consumer activations, launch events and promotional campaigns.
  • Track launch performance against agreed KPIs.
  • Gather consumer, retailer and distributor feedback and translate insights into actionable business improvements.
  • Continuously optimize products, pricing, distribution and marketing based on market performance.

Candidate Profile

We are looking for a commercially strong, proactive and execution-oriented FMCG professional with the ability to operate independently and build a business in a dynamic market.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 5+ years of relevant FMCG experience, preferably in food, dairy, ice cream, sauces, condiments, beverages, snacks or packaged foods.
  • Strong understanding of the Nepal FMCG market and consumer landscape.
  • Demonstrated experience in launching, developing or scaling FMCG brands in Nepal.
  • Practical knowledge of Nepal food regulations, product registration and labelling requirements.
  • Experience working with distributors, general trade, modern trade, supermarkets and/or HoReCa.
  • Experience in brand management, marketing, consumer activation and new product launches.
  • Strong commercial understanding of pricing, margins, trade economics and channel profitability.
  • Experience coordinating with manufacturers, suppliers and international principals.
  • Strong project management and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work independently, solve problems and take ownership from strategy through execution.

Preferred Experience

Preference will be given to candidates who have:

  • Successfully helped launch an Indian or international FMCG brand in Nepal.
  • Experience in ice cream, dairy, sauces, condiments or packaged foods.
  • Managed Nepal-side product registration and food regulatory compliance.
  • Built or developed brands during their early-stage market entry.
  • Established relationships with major Nepalese distributors, retailers and modern trade accounts.
  • Led new product launches and consumer activation programmes.
  • Worked directly with an international principal/manufacturer and a local Nepal operation.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a builder, not simply a brand custodian.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys creating businesses, making decisions and turning strategy into market execution.

You will have the opportunity to help determine:

What to launch → How to position it → How to localize it → How to make it compliant → How to price it → Where to distribute it → How to build consumer demand → How to scale the business.

You will serve as a key bridge between the Indian principal/company and the Nepal market, ensuring that the brand strategy, products and commercial model are effectively adapted to local market requirements.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to take significant ownership and responsibility for building a new FMCG business in Nepal, working with an established Indian brand and a growing portfolio across high-potential food categories.

If you are an entrepreneurial FMCG professional who understands the Nepal market, enjoys building brands and is comfortable taking an idea from concept to commercial execution, we would like to hear from you.

How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit their updated CV, along with a brief summary of their relevant FMCG brand-building, market development, or product launch experience in Nepal.

Please send your CV to: jawed.a@mvdugar.com

Alternatively, you may DM/WhatsApp: +977 9802537712

content.rendered:
Group of Helping Hands (SAHAS) Nepal is a non-profit making non-governmental-organization founded in 1996. Since then, SAHAS Nepal has been engaging in social mobilization, grassroots organisation/Community-Based Network Organisation (CBNO) formation and enhancing their capacity through partnership and implementing diverse programme and projects in the sectors of sustainable agriculture and food security, climate change, and education in 21 districts of Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal will be implementing an education project in Siraha district in Arnama and Bishnupur Rural Municipalities. The aim of the project is to enhance quality in education through an inclusive educational environment for children and improved livelihoods of parents in Siraha district. SAHAS Nepal is seeking energetic, committed and creative candidates to work on the education project aimed at enhancing the quality of education for the following positions, which will be based in Siraha district.

Position: Project Coordinator

Required no: 1

Academic Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, or a related field, with at least 5 years of relevant experience in the education sector, preferably Master’s degree with at least 3 years of relevant experience in the education sector
  • Proven project management experience, including planning, organizing, and managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating with Rural Municipalities, schools, teachers, and other education stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; ability to engage effectively with stakeholders at community, municipal, district, and provincial levels.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate, coach, and inspire project staff.
  • Knowledge of Nepal’s education system, policies, learning theories, and pedagogical strategies; familiarity with broader development work is an asset.
  • Prior experience working in rural communities, preferably in the Terai or similar geographic contexts.
  • Fluency in Maithili is highly preferred; strong command of Nepali and English (written and spoken).
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and basic data management tools.

Major Responsibilities

Project Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring

  • Lead overall project implementation in alignment with project goals, logframe, and detailed implementation plan.
  • Prepare annual, quarterly, and monthly work plans and ensure timely execution of activities as per project documents.
  • Collaborate with technical service providers to implement learning programs, training modules, and teaching–learning materials.
  • Manage project budgets, ensure expenditures comply with donor guidelines, and prepare budget reports as required by funding partners.
  • Track project progress, identify bottlenecks, document challenges and best practices, and recommend adaptive management actions.
  • Conduct regular field visits to assess program effectiveness, provide on-site coaching, and identify areas for improvement.

Coordination and Collaboration

  • Establish and maintain strong coordination with local government units (Rural Municipalities), education units, schools, teachers, and other relevant stakeholders at municipal, district, and provincial levels.
  • Liaise with project teams, partners, and key development facilitators to ensure smooth implementation and resource sharing.
  • Represent SAHAS Nepal at community, municipal, and district forums; ensure effective communication and cooperation with all stakeholders.
  • Facilitate community engagement activities to promote ownership and sustainability of project interventions.

Staff Mobilization, Monitoring, and Performance Review

  • Lead, mentor, and supervise project staff; provide regular coaching, capacity-building sessions, and performance feedback.
  • Mobilize staff according to project needs across Arnama and Bishnupur Rural Municipalities.
  • Conduct periodic performance reviews and support professional development of team members.

Report Writing and Documentation

  • Prepare timely progress reports (monthly, quarterly, annual) aligned with project goals and donor requirements.
  • Document key activities, lessons learned, case studies, and best practices for internal learning and external sharing.
  • Ensure proper filing and archiving of project documents, reports, and monitoring data.

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer

Required no: 1

Academic Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Development Studies, Social Science, Statistics, or a related field; Master’s preferred.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in M&E for education or development projects, preferably in rural or Terai contexts.
  • Strong experience with data collection and analysis tools (e.g., Kobo Toolbox, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, or similar).
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s education system, policies, and the broader development landscape.
  • Good computer skills (MS Office, especially Excel) and strong written and spoken English; Nepali required, Maithili preferred.
  • Experience designing surveys (baseline, midline, endline), indicators, and MEAL frameworks.
  • Strong analytical, reporting, and documentation skills; ability to translate data into actionable insights.

Major Responsibilities

Monitoring Planning and Indicator Development

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive Monitoring plan for the project.
  • Support the Project Coordinator in defining Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) at impact, outcome, output, and activity levels.
  • Ensure alignment of indicators with donor requirements and national education standards.

Data Management, Collection, and Analysis

  • Establish and maintain a project database to track progress against activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact.
  • Design and pilot data collection tools (surveys, checklists, feedback forms) for baseline, midline, and endline assessments.
  • Ensure accurate, timely, and ethical data collection, entry, cleaning, analysis, and visualization.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities in schools and communities and validate data quality.

Reporting, Documentation, and Learning

  • Generate periodic M&E reports (monthly, quarterly, annual) highlighting progress, trends, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Assist the Project Coordinator in preparing results-based reports of the project.
  • Document lessons learned, success stories, case studies, and best practices using text, photos, and video (with consent).
  • Organize capacity-building sessions for project staff on M&E tools, methodologies, and data use for decision-making.
  • Work closely with the project team to ensure all indicators are regularly monitored, reported, and used for adaptive management.

Position: Admin and Finance Assistant

Required Number: 1

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Studies (BBS), Business Administration (BBA), Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Minimum 1 year of relevant experience in finance, accounting, administration, procurement, or project support, preferably with an NGO/INGO or development organization.
  • Practical knowledge and experience in financial record keeping, bookkeeping, budget monitoring, procurement, and administrative management.
  • Good working knowledge of MS Excel, MS Word, PowerPoint, and accounting software.
  • Knowledge of government tax regulations, NGO financial procedures, donor compliance, and applicable organizational policies will be an advantage.
  • Good communication, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, integrity, and confidentiality in handling financial and administrative information.
  • Ability to work independently as well as effectively within a team and manage multiple tasks within deadlines.

Key Responsibilities

Finance and Accounting

  • Maintain day-to-day financial records and ensure accurate and timely recording of all financial transactions.
  • Maintain proper supporting documents, vouchers, bills, receipts, and other financial records in accordance compliance with organizational, government, and donor requirements.
  • Handle and maintain the project account and ensure proper documentation and reconciliation of project transactions.
  • Prepare periodic financial statements, expenditure reports, cash forecasts, and other financial information required by the project.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and identify variances for timely action.
  • Support the preparation, revision, and monitoring of the project budget in coordination with the Project Coordinator and relevant staff.
  • Ensure timely settlement of advances and maintain proper records of outstanding advances and liabilities.
  • Support internal and external audits and provide required financial documents and explanations.

Procurement and Logistics

  • Manage procurement-related processes in accordance with organizational procurement policies and donor requirements.
  • Obtain quotations, prepare procurement documentation, maintain supplier records, and ensure proper documentation of purchases.
  • Support the timely procurement and distribution of goods, materials, and services required for project implementation.
  • Maintain records of project assets, equipment, stock, and inventory.
  • Ensure the safe custody and appropriate use of project assets and materials.

Administration and Human Resources Support

  • Manage day-to-day administrative and logistical requirements of the project.
  • Maintain project-related personnel records, attendance, leave, contracts, and other administrative documents.
  • Ensure proper filing and safeguarding of administrative, financial, procurement, and personnel documents.

Coordination, Reporting and Compliance

  • Provide financial and administrative information required for project monitoring and reporting.
  • Perform other finance and administrative duties assigned by the supervisor in support of effective project implementation.

Position: Education Educator

Required Number: 2

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Minimum Intermediate level education; a Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Work, Development Studies, Sociology, or a related field will be preferred.
  • At least 1 year of relevant experience in community mobilization, education, child development, social development, or development projects.
  • Experience working with schools, teachers, parents, children/adolescents, community groups, and local government stakeholders will be an advantage.
  • Experience working in rural and marginalized communities, preferably in Madhesh Province or similar geographical and socio-cultural contexts.
  • Experience in facilitating community groups, training, orientation, meetings, and capacity-building activities.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, coordination, networking, and interpersonal skills.
  • Good report-writing and documentation skills with basic computer literacy, including MS Word and Excel.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong commitment to community participation, inclusion, child rights, gender equality, and quality education.
  • Ability to speak Maithili language is desirable.

Major Responsibilities

Community Mobilization and Group Strengthening

  • Work closely with parents, teachers, School Management Committees (SMCs), Female Community Health Volunteers (FCHVs), youth, community groups, local leaders and other stakeholders to promote quality education and improved livelihoods.
  • Facilitate the formation, strengthening, and institutional development of community-based groups.
  • Encourage community ownership and participation in education improvement and community development initiatives.

Education and School Support

  • Support schools and local stakeholders in addressing challenges related to school enrolment, attendance, retention, learning achievement, and quality of education.
  • Promote child-friendly, inclusive, gender-responsive, and participatory approaches to education.
  • Support schools and communities in implementing education improvement plans and project interventions.

Field Implementation and Coordination

  • Identify implementation challenges and facilitate effective communication between the project team, schools, communities, local government, and other stakeholders for timely action
  • Coordinate with relevant government offices, schools, community organizations, and local stakeholders to support project implementation.
  • Support the organization of training, workshops, meetings, campaigns, and other project events.

Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities, assess progress, and collect feedback from beneficiaries and stakeholders.
  • Assist in collecting and maintaining proper records of field activities, participants, achievements, challenges, and follow-up actions for monitoring, evaluation, and reporting purposes.
  • Support the M&E Officer in data collection, verification, monitoring, and documentation.

Position: Agriculture Technician

Required Number: 2

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Diploma in Agriculture from a recognized institution.
  • Minimum 1 year of relevant work experience in agriculture extension, climate-smart agriculture, community mobilization, agricultural production, or related development projects will be preferred.
  • Sound technical knowledge and practical experience in crop production, vegetable farming, soil management, livestock, climate-smart agriculture, farmer training, demonstrations, and working with farmer groups, communities, schools, and local government.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong commitment to teamwork, community participation and inclusion.
  • Good computer skills, including MS Word and Excel, and ability to prepare basic technical reports.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Agriculture Support

  • Provide technical support and facilitate training and demonstrations for farmers and community groups on crop production, vegetable farming, livestock management, sustainable and climate-smart agriculture, and improved farming technologies.
  • Support and train farmers and groups in planning and implementing seasonal agricultural activities and demonstrate appropriate agricultural technologies and best practices.
  • Provide technical support to schools and communities on climate-smart agriculture, food security, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and sustainable farming practices.
  • Promote linkages between agriculture, education, nutrition, food security, livelihoods, and life skills.

Community Group Formation and Capacity Development

  • Facilitate the formation and strengthening of community-based and farmer groups to develop their organizational capacity, leadership, planning, record keeping, and decision-making skills.
  • Facilitate preparation and implementation of agriculture-related plans developed by community groups.

Coordination and Linkages

  • Coordinate with local agriculture offices, livestock offices, ward offices, rural municipalities/municipalities, agricultural service providers, cooperatives, farmer groups, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with ward-level and local government authorities.
  • Facilitate linkages between community groups and relevant government agricultural extension services, technical institutions, markets, and service providers where appropriate.

Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

  • Regularly monitor and conduct follow up visits to agriculture-related activities, training, demonstrations, and field trials after implementation.
  • Prepare clear and timely reports after monitoring and field visits, highlighting progress, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations.
  • Maintain records of farmers/groups trained, technologies demonstrated, beneficiaries reached, and results achieved.

Salary and Benefits: As per the rules and regulations of SAHAS Nepal.

Practice Area: Governance
Bureau: Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific
Contract Duration: 1 Year
Required Languages: Fluency in English and Nepali.
Vacancy Timeline: 2 Weeks

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Project Description

Nepal adopted a new Constitution in September 2015, with the intent of transforming the then unitary and centralised system of governance into a federal and decentralised one as a vehicle to ensure equality, equity, and social justice. Nepal’s federal system is characterised by three levels of government (federal, provincial, and local) with non-hierarchical relationships within the levels of government. The Constitution stipulates that the three levels shall be the main structures of the Federal, Democratic and Republican Nepal and all levels shall exercise the power of state of Nepal pursuant to the Constitution and law. The powers of the three levels of government are enshrined in five Schedules of the constitution in the form of exclusive and concurrent powers. The federal system of governance became fully functional in February 2018 after all seven province governments were formed following the general election in November 2017.

With an objective to support on the implementation of federalism in Nepal, the Government of Nepal introduced a flagship programme of Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme (2019-2024). Following an initial period of delivery and agreement by GoN, Provinces, stakeholders, and Development Partners that Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme remained necessary and relevant, a decision was taken to extend Provincial and Local Governance Support Programme, with changes necessary to make the programme more effective, efficient, and responsive to the needs of Provincial Local Governments (PLG).

The Provincial and Local Governance Strengthening Programme (PLGSP) 2024-2029 is the national framework programme of the Government of Nepal (GoN) to build institutional, organizational, and individual capacity at all levels of government, with special focus on the provincial and local levels. It aims to attain functional, sustainable, inclusive, and accountable provincial and local governance. Following an initial period of delivery (2019-2023), and agreed by the GoN, Provinces, Development Partners, and other stakeholders, PLGSP will continue for the next five years, with necessary changes to make the programme more effective, efficient, and responsive to the emerging needs of PLGs in advancing federalism in Nepal.

An extensive stakeholder engagement, consultations and re-programming process was undertaken between July 2023 and June 2024 that resulting in a substantial revision in the PLGSP Programme Document (ProDoc). This reprogrammed ProDoc outlines how re-programmed PLGSP emphasizes building the capacity and capability of PLGs’ to deliver on the institutional and individual capacities for advancing federalism in Nepal over the next 5 years. The ProDoc has focused on three outcomes for Federal, Provincial and LG level impacts, each with three related outputs. Three outcomes include:  Outcome 1: Federal level government institutions and inter-governmental mechanisms are fully functional in support of federal governance as per the Constitution; Outcome 2: Provincial governments have efficient, effective, inclusive, and accountable institutions and organizations; Outcome 3: Local governments have capacity for Good Governance and for delivering inclusive basic services to all people. Furthermore, there are 9 outputs against the outcome mentioned. Four cross-cutting thematic streams: (i) Inclusive federalism acts, regulations, policies, and strategies; (ii) Collaboration within and across federal institutions and governments, and civic engagement; (iii) Supportive systems and tools for PLG inclusive federalism capacity; (iv) capacity development and transformation (applied to all 3 levels) have also been defined and articulated well.   The programme considers the broad principles and approaches including focus on federal devolution, transparency, and accountability, embedding transformative gender and diversity/inclusion agenda, human rights based and participatory approach, devolved, contextual and flexible programme design and implementation and adaptive programming. Further, unpacking structural barriers in political institutions, promoting ownership and trust in provincial and local government system and changing power dynamics in government institutions addressing intersectionality are the expected pathways for Gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) transformation in the programme. Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoFAGA) is the executing agency of the GoN for PLGSP in collaboration with the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers Provincial and Local Governments.

UNDP as the partner of PLGSP and Technical Assistance (TA) provider, has been working with the MoFAGA on the implementation of PLGSP since its inception. The TA component of the programme has also been revised accordingly to facilitate the transformation in the behaviours of the authorities towards federalism for inclusive service delivery, it is fully aligned with revised PLGSP incorporating learnings from the earlier TA engagement. The intent of the revised TA is to leverage UNDP’s technical expertise and facilitation role to support positive transformations that enable implementation of federalism in Nepal, ultimately contributing to more inclusive and effective delivery of inclusive services by PLGs to their people especially for the most marginalized and women.

To this effect, TA will support PLGs for their institutional and organizational capacities. The TA support to federal government will help develop and implement necessary laws and policies to strengthen inter-governmental relationships thereby supporting cooperative federalism. To attain the sustainable achievement described above, TA has been categorized into Implementation Support TA (ISTA) and Transformational TA. ISTA focuses more on supporting the governments in the implementation of PLGs thereby building their institutional and individual capacities. Whereas Transformational TA focuses more on supporting behavioural transformation through research and analysis as well as providing high level expertise as needed. Overall, the TA staff (ISTA and Transformational TA) works together in close coordination with each other in overall guidance of respective government and UNDP Country Office.

Position Summary:

The position holder has a key role in devising and demonstrating tools and systems on knowledge management so that PLGs (and all tires of the government) will be able to adopt those practices. The incumbent will also support the governments in adopting and devising those systems and adopt practices that bring all knowledge products in the repository to serve as institutional memory. S/he will also work in developing the communications strategy for PLGSP.

Scope of Work

The position contributes to all outputs of the programme.

1.Design and implementation of the Knowledge Management (KM) strategy:

  • Develop strategy for PLGs to document learnings and good practices support in its implementation so that PLGSP, Federal and PLGs have effective and sustainable systems to maintain and share knowledge and experience.
  • Support PLGSP management in the development of a communications strategy/guideline for PLGSP that will be applied across all units.
  • Identify new areas and analyze existing knowledge management support in activities.
  • Provide advice to PLGSP team in integrating knowledge management into their programme activities, including programme strategies, expert exchanges and communication.
  • Facilitate the development and dissemination of knowledge and experience through enhanced communication, strengthened knowledge products and publications.
  • Propose and promote creative solutions for knowledge management in the organization.
  • Support the Programme Coordination Unit (PCU) in integrating KM in all aspects of their operations.
  • Develop a system of a repository of information, knowledge and learning to track and systematically use the data.
  • Conduct peer-to-peer Learning (exchange, analysis and adaptation of knowledge/lessons learned/good practices) through dialogues, study visits, communities of practice.
  • Develop and maintain partnerships with external partners on their KM strategies.
  • Development of communication and visibility as well as KM tools and products

2.Strengthen the practice of knowledge exchange and sharing:

  • Identify knowledge management priorities related to products and media for dissemination, in coordination with government stakeholders.
  • Propose different modalities for peer-to-peer learning within the sector (webinar series, newsletter, communities of practice, collaboration tools, etc.) and elaborate formats for knowledge management products for e.g. the documentation of best practices and lessons learned in close coordination with the team.
  • Develop guidelines on community practices and support to implement it.
  • Conduct numbers of community of practices on diverse areas of federalism, governance and accountability.
  • Support Community of Practice (CoP) facilitators with skills building and with conceptual planning and implementation (as demanded) to ensure successful CoP.
  • Document the outcomes of the practices and share among wide range of stakeholders.

3.Ensure monitoring and reporting on knowledge management:

  • Review and monitor the KM budget and project in the concept of project management cycle.
  • Prepare KM and management analytical reports (including annual KM report and analyses).
  • Prepare and monitor web analytics of online tools.
  • Work with other members of the TA team to ensure high quality knowledge content is fed into these networks/events.
  • Produce radio programs on PBF projects/missions on various local and community radio stations for visibility and outreach.
  • Contribute to the analysis of technical information provided by the projects and synthesize it for the quarterly and annual reports, particularly regarding communication.

4.Introducing online knowledge management system:

  • Coordinate with IT and e-Governance Analyst on development of KM issues and online tools monitoring.
  • Identify, plan and organize training for PLGSP team on online tools usage to map and produce KM products.
  • Support capacity at all three tiers of government to design and implement effective communication and knowledge management strategies, contributing to increased participation, inclusion, engagement and awareness of PLGSP-supported processes.
  • Support to enhance PLGs capacities and support PLGs in producing high quality audio visuals and managing social media effectively for better visibility and engagement.
  • Strengthening outreach, communication and visibility of the programme.
  • Develop communication strategy of the programme, to ensure visibility of the programme activities at wider stakeholder level.
  • Document all the communication products and support to disseminate widely among the stakeholders.
  • Develop indicators to monitor and evaluate the progress of communications activities, to measure the impact on achieving the overall objectives (support the process of learning and innovation).
  • Monitor public perception, mass media and reports, at sector level and project level.
  • Produce newsletters and brochures on the various achievements, considering GESI based on lessons learned and success.
  • Support the design and operationalization of a website that will serve as the main information medium for the portfolio and as a forum for exchanging experiences between the various projects.

5.Ensuring strengthening GESI work through programme interventions:

  • Ensure transformative (GESI) approaches are integrated into the communications and knowledge management strategies and material.
  • Coordinate with GESI expert to produce GESI focused documentary, case studies etc.
  • Provide inputs on research and studies for mapping KM in GESI and in all three tiers of the government.
  • Provide advice to strengthen production of KM products in gender & social inclusion initiatives in the programme plan and implementation strategy.

Other:

  • Strictly Comply with the policies, strategies, code of conduct, guidelines on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA).
  • Strict compliance with the UNDP applicable rules, regulations and policies related to ethics and integrity.
  • The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the programme.

Institutional Arrangement

  • The Knowledge Management Analyst will report to and work under the direct supervision of the Federal Governance Specialist (International) and under the overall guidance of the National Programme Director (NPD) and the National Programme Manager (NPM).

Minimum Qualifications

Min. Education requirements

  • Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Communication, Journalism, International Relations, Sociology, Public Administration, or other relevant area is required. Or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields in combination with additional 2 years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

  • Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
  • Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience at the national level in public relations, advocacy, communications or knowledge management.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  • Experience and excellent knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point etc.) and web-based management and analytical tools.
  • Demonstrated experience in knowledge management and production of technical documents and materials, including policy briefs
  • Experience and knowledge of social media platforms and experience in social media outreach
  • Experience in communication related to governance and decentralization
  • Experience using graphic design and/or video editing software (Cf. Adobe Suite – Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects; Canva; etc.).
  • Experience in designing knowledge management strategies and operational plans
  • Experience in online communications tools and awareness campaigns.
  • Experience in public relations and external communication, dissemination campaigns and awareness-raising
  • Proven ability to deliver oral presentations to various audiences is desired
  • Experience and good knowledge of gender issues.
  • Experience of undertaking independent desk research and writings on topics relevant to governance
  • Experience of producing various written communications products and working with media technology, web-based management systems, social media for public information/advocacy
  • Experience of translating technical information into a wide variety of target groups

Required Language(s)

  • Fluency in English and Nepali is required.
  • Working knowledge of any other national language will be an added advantage.

Job Description

This is a roster recruitment. The selected candidate can be placed in Kathmandu or any provincial offices within Nepal as per the requirement

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Administration and Finance Analyst will be responsible for the day-to-day financial management, administration, and operational support of the project. The Analyst ensures the effective and transparent utilization of financial resources, compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, and integrates principles of Gender Equality, Social Inclusion (GESI), and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) into all operational activities.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure implementation of Financial Management and Accounting

  • Manage the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and NIM/DIM procedures.
  • Process payment requests, disbursements, and travel claim accurately within the UNDP ERP system (e.g., Quantum).
  • Maintain a robust internal expenditure control system. Regularly monitor financial exception reports, investigate unusual transactions or anomalies, and propose corrective actions to management.
  • Continuously monitor project budgets and expenditures in cooperation with the Project Manager.
  • Conduct quality financial analysis of budget performance by cost inputs and partners and support the preparation of financial forecasts and disbursement requests.
  • Prepare timely and accurate financial statements, bank reconciliations, and consolidated reports for the Project Board, donors, and the Country Office.
  • Support the development of funding requests, grant negotiations, and amendments.
  • Facilitate programme audits and investigations in coordination with relevant oversight bodies.
  • Ensure the effective implementation of audit recommendations, management actions, and recovery actions.
  • Conduct regular field visits in close coordination with the programme team to ensure financial compliance and provide monitoring support for implementing partners and sub-recipients.

Ensure management of programme budgets and the operation of the optimal cost recovery system

  • Prepare, continuously monitor, and revise programme budgets in UNDP ERP systems (Quantum and Hyperion), ensuring strict alignment with approved detailed budgets and Annual Work Plans (AWPs).
  • Implement optimal cost recovery mechanisms, ensuring Direct Project Costs (DPC) and General Management Support (GMS) fees are accurately calculated and billed.
  • Maintain robust internal controls to ensure transactions are correctly coded against budget lines and donor agreements prior to approval.
  • Conduct regular analysis of budget delivery and expenditure variances.
  • Prepare budget reviews, financial forecasts, and provide justifications for necessary budget reallocations or reprogramming requests for submission to donors.
  • Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual cash flow forecasts.
  • Monitor incoming donor contributions, ensuring the timely transfer, identification, and registration of receipts in the system.
  • Finalize the financial sections of progress reports, disbursement requests, and statements of sources and use of funds, strictly adhering to specific donor reporting timelines and requirements.
  • Transaction Processing & Records Management: Manage the initiation, approval, and settlement of bank transfers.
  • Ensure the proper management of cash receipts and petty cash, and maintain a rigorous, audit-ready filing system for all finance records and documents.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in monitoring and evaluation

  • In coordination with the Project Manager supports the development of partnerships and maintains strong working relationships with the national, provincial partners and entities, donors, technical partners, and UN agencies to ensure transparent and effective management, quality services and oversight of the programmes.
  • Supports the Project Manager in the development of capacity development through different trainings/coaching/mentoring and transition strategies to support national entities to implement and assume the PR role, ensuring access to appropriate tools and resources.
  • Actively participates in UNDP and other relevant external networks/forums to promote the programme.
  • Conduct training for the project and other relevant stakeholders on financial management and oversight.

Ensure Effective Administration and Operations Management

  • Ensure the effective administration and operational management of the project in compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.
  • Coordinate project procurement activities, including preparation of procurement plans, specifications, requests for quotations, purchase orders, and contract management in accordance with UNDP procurement policies.
  • Monitor the implementation of procurement activities and maintain an updated procurement tracking system to ensure timely delivery of goods and services.
  • Support recruitment processes for project personnel and consultants, including preparation of Terms of Reference (TORs), evaluation processes, contract administration, and onboarding arrangements.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements for project personnel, consultants, and stakeholders, including travel authorizations, ticketing, logistics, security clearances, and travel claim settlements.
  • Organize project meetings, workshops, trainings, and field missions, ensuring appropriate logistical, administrative, and financial arrangements.
  • Maintain project asset and inventory records and ensure proper utilization, maintenance, verification, transfer, and disposal of project assets in accordance with UNDP policies.
  • Ensure effective records management and maintain an organized filing system for project administrative, procurement, human resources, and operational documentation.
  • Monitor the validity and timely renewal of project contracts, agreements, leases, and service arrangements.
  • Support the preparation and monitoring of project work plans, procurement plans, HR plans, and operational plans.
  • Coordinate with UNDP operations units and service providers to ensure timely provision of administrative and operational support services.
  • Identify operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures to ensure efficient project implementation.
  • Support project closure activities, including asset disposal, records archiving, contract closure, and administrative reporting.
  • Ensure environmental sustainability, accessibility, safeguarding, and GESI considerations are integrated into project operations and administrative processes.

Contribution towards Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)

  • Ensure GESI is mainstreamed in the budget, Annual Work Plan (AWP), procurement and HR plans, and all other administrative work to be undertaken by the project in coordination with Community, Rights and Gender Analyst and GESI Analyst of UNDP CO.
  • Promote gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) throughout programme implementation.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.
  • Promote a respectful, inclusive, and safe workplace culture, supporting “Do No Harm” principles in all administrative and field-level operations.
  • Assist in collecting and reporting gender-disaggregated data related to project administration, procurements, and event participation.
  • The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

  • A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced (master’s) University Degree in Finance and/or Accounting is required.
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Finance and/or Accounting in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.
  • Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.
  • Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.
  • Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).
  • Candidates with MBA or master’s in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Min. years of relevant work experience

  • Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
  • Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of working experience in administration and finance.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  • Experience managing donor-funded projects, preferably with UN agencies, international organizations, or development partners, including collaboration with implementing partners, government entities, NGOs, and sub-recipients.
  • Experience supporting audits, investigations, and implementation of audit recommendations.
  • Proven experience in financial reporting, budget preparation, monitoring, cash flow forecasting, and expenditure analysis, in line with donor and organizational requirements.

  • Experience coordinating administrative and operational activities for multi-stakeholder projects.
  • Experience organizing workshops, meetings, trainings, conferences, and field missions.

  • Solid experience in working with a multi-cultured group of people and systems in high-pressure environments
  • Familiar with dealing with client relationships with international organizations, national governments and civil society
  • Demonstrated ability to ensure compliance with financial regulations, internal control procedures, and audit standards.

Position: Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer
Organization: Debate Network Nepal (DNN)
Duty Station: Kathmandu, Nepal
Reports To: National Program Coordinator
Contract Duration: Until 31 December 2028, with an initial three-month probation period
Employment Type: Full-time
Salary: NRs. 45,000/- (Negotiable)

1. Background

Debate Network Nepal (DNN) is a youth-led organization established in 2013 that works to strengthen critical thinking, public speaking, democratic dialogue, and meaningful youth participation in Nepal. Through debate education, training, advocacy, community engagement, and creative learning approaches, DNN supports young people to become informed, confident, and active contributors to society.

DNN has engaged more than 12,000 young people across Nepal through debate, facilitation, youth leadership, civic engagement, and learning initiatives. The organization works with youth networks, educational institutions, civil-society organizations, local governments, and other stakeholders to create inclusive spaces for dialogue, learning, advocacy, and youth-led action.

DNN is a key implementing partner in the Reclaiming Advocacy through Narratives, Debates, Grassroots Theatre and Arts (RANGA) Project, implemented in consortium with Mandala Theatre Nepal and Campaign for Change. The RANGA Project promotes youth engagement through culture and creativity, using theatre, debate, storytelling, and digital media to empower young people as creators, advocates, and active citizens.

The project integrates gender equality, social inclusion, and the “leave no one behind” principle. It particularly seeks to engage marginalized young people, including Dalit and Indigenous communities, persons with disabilities, gender-diverse individuals, and LGBTIQ+ communities, including intersex persons.

2. Purpose of the Position

The Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer will provide administrative, financial, documentation, and operational support for Debate Network Nepal’s programs, projects, and organizational activities. The position will ensure effective, compliant, timely, and well-documented implementation of DNN activities in accordance with approved work plans, budgets, organizational policies, and donor requirements.

While the RANGA Project will be a primary assignment, the Officer will also support DNN’s other ongoing and future programs, including debate education, youth engagement, trainings, events, advocacy initiatives, partnerships, and organizational operations.

The position will work closely with the National Program Coordinator, Managing Director, program team, Provincial Coordinators, consultants, and consortium partners. The Officer will support financial management, procurement, documentation systems, communication and visibility documentation, monitoring and evaluation, and technical and financial reporting across DNN’s work.

3. Key Responsibilities

The Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer will support the RANGA Project as a primary assignment and will also provide administrative, financial, and documentation support to other DNN programs and organizational activities, as assigned by DNN management.

3.1 Financial Management

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records for RANGA and other DNN projects, programs, and organizational expenditures.
  • Prepare payment vouchers, maintain ledger entries, coordinate bank reconciliations, and ensure timely processing of payments.
  • Track budget utilization and provide regular financial updates to the National Program Coordinator, Managing Director, and relevant project teams.
  • Ensure expenditures comply with approved budget lines, DNN financial procedures, donor regulations, and applicable legal requirements.
  • Support the preparation of project-wise and organizational financial summaries for interim, annual, and final reporting.
  • Maintain organized physical and digital filing systems for financial documentation.
  • Support internal and external audits, financial reviews, and donor verification processes.
  • Assist in preparing budget forecasts, budget revisions, and financial inputs for proposals and new project planning, as assigned.

3.2 Administrative and Operational Support

  • Provide administrative and logistical support for DNN workshops, debates, trainings, theatre events, fellowships, meetings, advocacy activities, and organizational events.
  • Support procurement processes in line with DNN policies, donor requirements, and applicable procedures.
  • Prepare and maintain contracts, consultancy agreements, partnership documents, letters, meeting minutes, and administrative correspondence.
  • Maintain DNN’s asset register, inventory records, and related documentation.
  • Support travel arrangements, travel advances, reimbursements, and settlement documentation for staff, consultants, participants, and provincial activities.
  • Coordinate administrative communication within the Kathmandu office and with Provincial Coordinators, consultants, and partners.
  • Support office operations, record keeping, filing, and other administrative systems necessary for smooth organizational functioning.

3.3 Documentation, Communication, and Reporting Support

  • Maintain systematic documentation of DNN program and project activities, including attendance sheets, reports, photographs, case studies, participant outputs, and event materials.
  • Support the compilation, formatting, review, and submission of narrative, technical, and progress reports for RANGA and other DNN projects.
  • Coordinate with Provincial Coordinators and program teams to collect, verify, and organize timely reporting inputs.
  • Support communication and visibility work by organizing approved photographs, stories, testimonials, videos, event information, and other materials for newsletters, social media, websites, reports, and donor visibility products.
  • Ensure secure, accessible, and properly organized physical and digital archives, in accordance with DNN policies and donor requirements.
  • Support the preparation of organizational profiles, presentations, program summaries, and documentation needed for external communication, partnerships, and proposal development.

3.4 Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning Support

  • Support data collection for project indicators, participant records, and beneficiary tracking across DNN programs.
  • Maintain updated beneficiary databases with required disaggregation, including gender, age, inclusion categories, location, and project-specific indicators.
  • Assist in compiling monitoring reports, participant feedback, learning documentation, and evidence of outcomes.
  • Support periodic program reviews, reflection meetings, monitoring visits, and learning processes by providing relevant documentation and data.
  • Contribute to evidence-based documentation of DNN’s program results, learning, and impact.

3.5 Compliance and Safeguarding Support

  • Support compliance with DNN policies, donor regulations, procurement procedures, financial controls, safeguarding standards, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) principles, and data-protection requirements.
  • Ensure secure handling and confidential storage of financial, participant, personnel, and safeguarding-sensitive documents.
  • Flag documentation, financial, procedural, or compliance gaps to the National Program Coordinator or Managing Director in a timely manner.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and ethical conduct in all administrative and financial processes.

4. Deliverables

  • Monthly financial tracking, expenditure updates, and complete supporting documentation for RANGA and assigned DNN activities.
  • Updated administrative, financial, contractual, asset, and procurement files.
  • Consolidated activity documentation and reporting inputs from Kathmandu and provincial programs.
  • Updated participant, beneficiary, and monitoring-and-evaluation tracking databases.
  • Timely support to interim, annual, and final technical and financial reports for DNN projects.
  • Organized communication and visibility documentation, including approved stories, photographs, testimonials, and event materials.
  • Support for audits, donor compliance checks, proposal budgets, organizational documentation, and other tasks assigned by DNN management.

5. Duration and Contract Conditions

  • The contract will be valid until 31 December 2028, subject to satisfactory performance, organizational need, project continuity, and availability of funding.
  • The position will have an initial three-month probation period. Continuation beyond probation will be subject to a performance review.
  • This is a full-time position based in Kathmandu.
  • Occasional travel within Nepal may be required for DNN programs, project activities, monitoring visits, partner coordination, or organizational events.

6. Reporting and Supervision

  • The Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer will report directly to the National Program Coordinator and will work closely with:
  • Managing Director and DNN’s Kathmandu-based program and operations team.
  • Provincial Coordinators and facilitators for financial documentation, activity reporting, and data consolidation.
  • Consortium partners, including Mandala Theatre Nepal and Campaign for Change, for RANGA-related coordination and reporting.
  • Consultants, vendors, service providers, and relevant stakeholders, as required for administrative and program operations.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Development Studies, or a related field.

Experience

  • Minimum of two year of relevant experience in administration, finance, procurement, logistics, documentation, accounting, or operations support in an NGO, INGO, development project, donor-funded project, or similar organization.
  • Demonstrated experience managing procurement and logistics for trainings, workshops, events, field activities, travel, and office operations.
  • Experience handling financial documentation, including payment vouchers, bills, invoices, quotations, comparative statements, advance settlements, and supporting documentation for audits.
  • Practical familiarity with taxation related to goods, services, consultancy payments, rent, staff salary, and other human-resource-related payments in Nepal.
  • Experience supporting compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, procurement procedures, and financial controls.
  • Experience with multi-partner, multi-province, or consortium projects will be an advantage.

Skills and Competencies

  • Demonstrated practical experience in procurement and logistics management within the development, NGO, INGO, donor-funded project, or social-sector context.
  • Sound knowledge of procurement processes, including collecting quotations, preparing comparative analyses, supporting vendor selection, preparing purchase orders, maintaining procurement files, and ensuring compliance with organizational and donor procedures.
  • Experience coordinating logistics for trainings, workshops, events, field visits, meetings, travel, accommodation, transport, venue arrangements, participant reimbursements, and material distribution.
  • Working knowledge of Nepal’s taxation requirements relevant to organizational and project operations, including VAT, Tax Deducted at Source (TDS), withholding tax, and applicable tax deductions for goods, services, consultancy fees, rent, transport, and other operational expenses.
  • Practical experience calculating, deducting, depositing, and maintaining documentation for taxes applicable to procurement of goods and services.
  • Familiarity with human-resource-related taxation, including salary tax, TDS on staff and consultant payments, CIT, provident fund contributions where applicable, and related payroll documentation.
  • Ability to prepare or support the preparation of tax records, payment vouchers, invoices, bills, PAN/VAT verification documents, tax clearance-related documents, and supporting files for audits.
  • Knowledge of financial documentation procedures, including payment vouchers, advance settlements, bank reconciliations, cashbook and ledger maintenance, expense verification, and financial filing.
  • Ability to ensure that expenditures comply with approved budgets, procurement thresholds, donor requirements, DNN financial policies, and relevant laws of Nepal.
  • Experience maintaining asset registers, inventory records, stock records, handover forms, and documentation for purchased goods and equipment.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including preparing budget trackers, expenditure reports, procurement comparison sheets, payment calculations, tax deductions, and financial summaries.

8. How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates should submit the following documents:

  • A cover letter explaining their interest in the position and relevant experience.
  • An updated CV, including contact details for at least two professional references.
  • Copies of relevant academic certificates and citizenship/identity document.

Please send your application by email to debate.dnn@gmail.com with the subject line: Application for Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer

Application Deadline: 05 September 2026

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the selection process.

DNN encourages applications from women, Dalit and Indigenous communities, persons with disabilities, gender-diverse persons, LGBTIQ+ individuals, and other marginalized groups.

9. Ethical Standards

The position holder must adhere to:

  • DNN’s Code of Conduct.
  • Anti-discrimination, equity, and inclusion principles.
  • Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) principles.
  • Safeguarding and confidentiality requirements.
  • Transparency, accountability, and ethical financial-management standards.
